value_or_angle: header="Shot at the Derby Line Hotel" body="On 31 August 1876 Edwin Hayden came to the Derby Line Hotel, where Gertrude was staying with her sister Clara. He shot Clara's husband, then shot Gertrude as she cried out, “Oh, Edwin.” She died on 6 September, at twenty-three." category=death
status: OK nb_approved appended verbatim: 'Shot at the Derby Line Hotel'

value_or_angle: header="The belle of Derby Line" body="The acknowledged belle of Derby Line, Gertrude married Edwin Hayden at Boston in 1871 over her family's objections, just after coming into an inheritance. Her money set him up in a Boston corset factory, which burned in the fire of 1872." category=marriage
status: OK nb_approved appended verbatim: 'The belle of Derby Line'

value_or_angle: header="She left him in 1875" body="Her money went next into a hotel he kept at Stanstead, and was spent there. In 1875, after years of beatings, Gertrude left him for a sister at Allston, near Boston, and would not go back while he drank." category=marriage
status: OK nb_approved appended verbatim: 'She left him in 1875'

value_or_angle: header="What she said before she died" body="Before she died Gertrude said her husband had often knocked her down, and had once forced her to sign over bonds by threatening to shoot her." category=death
status: OK nb_approved appended verbatim: 'What she said before she died'

value_or_angle: header="Hanged at Windsor in 1881" body="Convicted of first-degree murder in September 1877, Edwin spent more than three years in the state prison at Windsor and was hanged there on 25 February 1881. On the scaffold he denied ever abusing his wife and blamed her family." category=death
status: OK nb_approved appended verbatim: 'Hanged at Windsor in 1881'

value_or_angle: header="His last plea failed at Montpelier" body="A legislative committee sent new evidence to the judges, and Governor Farnham reprieved him to February. On 16 February 1881 the court ruled he had been as sane as ever men are in committing such crimes." category=law
status: OK nb_approved appended verbatim: 'His last plea failed at Montpelier'

value_or_angle: header="A paymaster's clerk in 1864" body="Born at Cincinnati, Edwin was raised partly by his grandfather Russel Perry at Montpelier and went to Barre Academy. In 1864 he joined the Union army as an assistant paymaster, under his guardian, General Pitkin." category=military
status: OK nb_approved appended verbatim: 'A paymaster's clerk in 1864'

value_or_angle: header="Corsets in Boston, a hotel at Stanstead" body="After clerking for Jordan, Marsh and travelling for Champney Brothers, Edwin started a Boston corset factory with his wife's money; it burned in the 1872 fire. He then kept the Studdert Hotel at Stanstead, Quebec." category=business

value_or_angle: header="Shot through the lung for his sister-in-law" body="On 31 August 1876 Charles barred Edwin Hayden from his wife's sister Gertrude at the Derby Line Hotel, and Hayden shot him through the lung before killing her. Charles recovered and testified at the trial." category=family
